metadata.blurb: Brave Wallet is Brave's browser-native self-custody wallet.

ref.explanation: Brave Wallet creation asks users to back up a 12-word recovery phrase for self-custody wallet access.
Brave Wallet supports Web3 dapp use and address entry, but no ENS resolution feature evidence was found in the public wallet help pages.
Targeted review of Brave Wallet help and release notes found no user-facing ENS recipient-resolution documentation.
Brave Wallet advertises wallet-native swaps and cross-chain asset management from the browser wallet.
Brave Wallet says users can buy, store, send, swap, and manage crypto assets and NFTs in one wallet.
Brave Wallet is built into Brave Browser and connects to Web3 dapps without an extension.
Brave Browser, including Brave Wallet source, is published in the brave-browser repository under the MPL-2.0 license.
Brave Wallet supports creating a wallet from a recovery phrase and managing accounts inside the browser wallet.
Brave's privacy policy says users can switch off automatic usage statistics and crash reports, implying optional crash-report collection.
Brave's privacy policy describes privacy-preserving product analytics and an option to disable automatic usage statistics.
Brave release notes credit wallet security fixes reported through HackerOne, indicating Brave's HackerOne security program covers wallet issues.
Brave Wallet creation requires setting a password for the wallet.
Brave Wallet's feature matrix says desktop Brave Wallet can connect and securely sign transactions with hardware wallets like Ledger and Trezor.
Brave Wallet public docs describe RPC-backed wallet network access and custom networks, but no embedded Ethereum L1 light-client verification path was found.
Brave Wallet help and release notes reviewed for this entry did not show a malicious-contract registry warning feature comparable to Blockaid-style alerts.
Brave Browser has phishing protection, but wallet-specific public docs did not show wallet connection warnings for known-malicious dapps.
Brave Wallet public docs did not show risky-recipient or transaction-risk warning support before signing.
Brave Wallet public docs reviewed for this entry did not show transaction simulation previews before signing.

Brave Wallet feature docs and support pages reviewed for this entry show dapp, swap, custom network, hardware-wallet, and portfolio features, but no native token-approval inventory or revoke workflow.
Brave Wallet's feature matrix says users can add custom EVM-compatible networks by entering standardized network IDs and values.
Brave Browser GitHub releases use GitHub's release pipeline and publish signed release assets/checksums through the browser release process.
Brave publishes release notes for browser and wallet changes.
Brave publishes source and build instructions, but no wallet-specific reproducible-build attestation for end-user releases was found.
Brave Wallet is built into Brave desktop browser and Brave feature matrix lists Desktop, iOS, and Android wallet support.
Brave Wallet is built into the Brave browser rather than distributed as a standalone desktop wallet app.
Brave feature matrix lists iOS and Android wallet support.
Brave Wallet is browser-native and built into Brave, not installed as a separate extension.
Brave Wallet is built into the Brave desktop browser.
Brave Wallet is built natively into the Brave browser, not offered as a standalone browser-based web app usable without installing Brave.
Brave feature matrix includes iOS support.
Brave feature matrix includes Android support.
Brave Wallet is built into Brave browser, not Chrome.
Brave Wallet is built into Brave browser, not Firefox.
Brave Wallet is built into Brave browser, not Safari.
Brave Wallet feature matrix lists EVM-compatible network support, Solana support, and NFT transactions on Solana and Ethereum.
Brave Wallet supports custom EVM-compatible networks and Ethereum/EVM dApps.
Brave Wallet supports Solana swaps and NFT transactions on Solana.
Brave Wallet natively supports Bitcoin, letting users create Bitcoin accounts and send/receive native BTC across Legacy, SegWit, and Taproot address types.
Brave Wallet's supported networks (Ethereum/EVM, Solana, Filecoin, Bitcoin, Zcash, Cardano) do not include Cosmos SDK/IBC chains.
TON is not among Brave Wallet's supported networks listed by Brave.
Sui is not among Brave Wallet's supported networks.
Aptos is not supported; community reports confirm Brave Wallet cannot be used with Aptos apps/bridges.
Brave Wallet does not support the XRP Ledger, as confirmed by community reports that XRP cannot be stored in Brave Wallet.
Brave and Input|Output completed native Cardano integration, letting users hold and manage ADA and Cardano native assets, send/receive, and swap directly in the wallet.
Brave Wallet feature matrix lists dApp support for Ethereum and EVM-compatible networks across desktop, iOS, and Android.
Brave Wallet supports dApps through Brave browser surfaces.
Brave Wallet provides direct dApp support for Ethereum/EVM networks, not WalletConnect-only access.
Brave Wallet feature matrix lists off-ramps on desktop and Brave blog describes a fiat-crypto on-ramp for US users.
Brave announced a fiat-crypto on-ramp for Brave Wallet.
Brave feature matrix lists off-ramps for crypto-to-fiat in select countries.

Ramp supports bank transfers (SEPA/Easy Bank Transfer/manual transfers) per its payment-methods page, and Brave's off-ramp blog confirms bank transfers are among Ramp's supported methods in Brave Wallet.
Ramp Network (Brave Wallet's integrated on/off-ramp) supports Visa/Mastercard debit and credit cards per Ramp's official payment-methods support page.
Ramp supports Apple Pay (with a linked Visa/Mastercard), as confirmed by Ramp's payment-methods page and Brave's own off-ramp blog stating Ramp integrates Apple Pay.
Ramp supports Google Pay (with a linked Visa/Mastercard) per Ramp's official payment-methods page, and Brave's off-ramp blog lists Google Pay among Ramp's integrated methods.

fiatRamps.regionalAvailability: Brave feature matrix says off-ramps are available in select countries.

Brave Wallet supports standard EVM transaction sending where gas settings can be inspected or controlled in the wallet flow.
Brave Wallet is a traditional EOA wallet with no account abstraction layer; official sources show no paymaster or dApp gas sponsorship.
Brave Wallet is a traditional EOA wallet; official pages describe standard gas fees with no account abstraction, paymasters, or gasless UX.
Brave Wallet's gas documentation describes only native-token gas payments with no stablecoin gas option.
Brave Wallet support/product materials include stuck or pending transaction recovery guidance.

Brave Wallet onboarding uses a password plus seed-phrase creation/import, with no passkey/WebAuthn signup option.
Onboarding does not require or offer email signup; users only set a password and create/import a seed phrase.
Brave Wallet is a self-custody wallet created via seed phrase, with no no-seed embedded/MPC/smart-account social-login option.
Brave Wallet feature matrix describes storing, managing, growing, swapping a crypto portfolio and market data, custom tokens, and NFT transactions.
Brave Wallet lets users manage a crypto portfolio from the wallet.
Brave Wallet's portfolio shows token balances, market prices and trends (via CoinGecko) but there is no profit/loss tracking documented on its features page.
No cost-basis/acquisition-cost tracking is described in Brave Wallet's official features or portfolio documentation; it only displays current balances and prices.
Brave Wallet supports custom tokens and market data.
Brave feature matrix lists NFT transactions on Solana and Ethereum.
Brave announced an NFT gallery for Brave Wallet.

Brave Wallet's official import options cover only recovery phrase, private key, and JSON keystore imports, with no documented ability to add a public address as a watch-only/view-only account; the internal 'Watch-Only' NFT label merely flags unowned NFTs rather than a deliberate watch-address feature.
Brave Wallet lets users add and manage multiple accounts (including imported MetaMask/Ledger/Trezor accounts) across chains in one portfolio view.

Brave announced an NFT gallery for viewing and managing NFT collections.
Brave feature matrix lists NFT transactions, including send and receive NFTs.

No Brave Wallet documentation indicates it surfaces lending/borrowing positions (Aave, Compound, etc.); it only shows wallet token balances.
Brave Wallet displays token/NFT balances and prices only; there is no documented feature that surfaces staking positions held in external DeFi protocols.
Brave Wallet does not document any reading of liquidity-pool positions; its portfolio is limited to token and NFT balances.
No documentation shows Brave Wallet surfacing yield-vault positions such as Yearn or Morpho.
Brave Wallet does not document surfacing of claimable DeFi rewards from external protocols.
With no DeFi borrow-position awareness in the wallet, there are no documented liquidation-risk warnings.

Brave Wallet offers no in-app liquid staking; users are advised only to manually swap to LSTs like stSOL as a workaround, not an integrated feature.
Validator selection is only part of the unimplemented native-staking feature request, so it is not available in Brave Wallet.
With no in-app staking/earn product, Brave Wallet does not display staking/earn APY.
No in-app staking exists, so there is no in-app rewards-claiming functionality in Brave Wallet.
